question: In a skewed smooth distribution with a tail exended to the left, the statistic with the highest value is the
options: median

model_outputs: A skewed distribution with a tail extended to the left is known as a left-skewed or negatively skewed distribution. In a left-skewed distribution, the tail is longer on the left side, meaning that there are more extreme values on the left side. The mode is the value that appears most frequently in the data set, and it is not necessarily affected by the skewness of the distribution. The mean is also affected by the skewness of the distribution. The range is the difference between the highest and lowest values in the data set. The mean, median, and mode are all measures of central tendency, while the quartile deviation, interquartile range, variance, and standard deviation are measures of variability. The geometric mean and harmonic mean are also measures of central tendency, but they are more commonly used for skewed distributions. In a left-skewed distribution, the mean is typically lower than the median, and the mode is typically lower than the mean. The range is the highest value in a left-skewed distribution. The answer is (F).
